title: Good Works and Salvation
definition: Good Works and Salvation teaches that good works do not earn salvation but necessarily flow from saving grace.
summary: Good Works and Salvation clarifies that works do not earn salvation but necessarily follow saving grace.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves His people for a life of obedience, holiness, service, and love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine holds together two truths: believers are not saved by works, and those who are saved are created for good works. Works are fruit, evidence, and service—not the root of acceptance with God. It protects the Gospel from legalism and protects discipleship from laziness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because churches often drift into either performance-based religion or grace without transformation. Scripture refuses both errors. Good works display God's workmanship and bless others while keeping Christ as the ground of salvation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do good works as grateful obedience, not as a payment plan. Examine whether your life shows the fruit of grace. Encourage believers to serve without letting service become their identity before God.
